rule_metadata.description: The dedicated module for Madd Munfasil, covering the 4-to-5 count separated lengthening that occurs when a Madd letter ends one word and a Hamzah begins the next word, complete with a 40-question assessment bank.

theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: Madd Munfasil occurs when a Madd letter (Alif, Waw, or Ya) appears at the very end of a word, and the immediately succeeding word begins with a Hamzah (ء).
theoretical_foundation.ruling_and_duration: Extended for **4 to 5 counts** (Harakat) according to the standard narration of Hafs 'an 'Asim (via Shatibiyyah route).
theoretical_foundation.permissible_shortening: In certain authentic scholarly transmission paths (Turuq), it is permissible to shorten it to 2 counts (Qasr al-Munfasil), though 4-5 counts remains standard practice.
theoretical_foundation.wasl_vs_waqf: Munfasil applies only when connecting words in recitation (Wasl). If you pause (Waqf) on the first word ending with the Madd letter, it reduces to a standard 2-count Madd Tabii because the succeeding Hamzah is temporarily cut off.
theoretical_foundation.mushaf_indicator: A wavy Maddah sign (~) placed over the final Madd letter of the first word.

practical_examples.breakdown: Alif Madd at end of 'Bima' meets Hamzah at start of 'unzila'; extended 4-5 counts.
Alif Madd at end of 'Ya' meets Hamzah at start of 'ayyuha'; extended 4-5 counts.
Waw Madd at end of 'Qalu' meets Hamzah at start of 'amanna'.
